wiki_text: In May 2026, B.Grimm Power (Thailand) and PetroVietnam Power Corporation (PV Power) signed a cooperation agreement to develop the Vung Ang III LNG-fired power project, and in June 2026 the Ha Tinh Provincial People's Committee approved the project's investment policy and its investor consortium of PV Power (51%), B.Grimm Power (34%) and Vietnam Machinery Installation Corporation (Lilama). The VND 51.43 trillion (~US$2 billion) project in Hoanh Son ward comprises two 750 MW units on about 51.7 ha of land and 16 ha of sea surface, with unit 1 expected to enter commercial operation in Q1 2031 and unit 2 in Q2 2032.

topic: Downstream LNG supply to the Quang Trach power complex
wiki_text: PetroVietnam Gas (PV Gas) plans to supply regasified LNG from the Vung Ang terminal in Ha Tinh province to the nearby Quang Trach power complex in Quang Tri province, including the Quang Trach 2 and Quang Trach 3 gas-fired power plants, with gas deliveries scheduled to begin from April 2029. The gas is delivered by pipeline as regasified LNG, so the marine LNG import for these power plants takes place at the Vung Ang terminal rather than at the power-plant sites.

On February 12, 2026, the Nghe An Provincial People's Committee approved the investment and the investor consortium for the Quynh Lap LNG power project (Decision No. 26/QD-UBND): PetroVietnam Power Corporation (PV Power), SK Innovation (South Korea) and Nghe An Sugar Co., Ltd. (NASU). Construction of technical infrastructure began on May 18, 2026. The ~US$2.25 billion project in Quynh Lap commune, Hoang Mai township comprises a 1,500 MW plant (two CCGT units), a gas receiving terminal for carriers of about 100,000 DWT and an LNG input of about 1.15 million tonnes per year, targeting commercial operation by December 2030.

Under the schedule reported from provincial project meetings in October-November 2024, the Hai Lang LNG phase 1 consortium (T&T Group 40%, KOGAS 20%, KOSPO 20%, Hanwha Energy 20%) planned to establish the project company and complete feasibility approval in late 2025, sign the EPC contract in Q4 2025 (48-month build), begin construction around January 2026, and reach commercial operation by December 31, 2029 (trial operation from April 2029). Phase 1 includes an LNG terminal receiving 170,000-226,000 m3 carriers with a capacity of 1.5 million tonnes per year. As of the latest verified reporting the project remained pre-construction.

Da Nang added the VND 5,429 billion (~US$209 million) LNG/LPG berth project at the Lien Chieu port area to its investment-attraction list in May 2025 (about 62.3 ha, two LNG/LPG berths for 10,000-100,000 DWT vessels in the first phase and four more liquid-cargo berths planned after 2030). As of mid-2026 no investor had been selected for the LNG/LPG berth; the March 2026 Lien Chieu investor award (Hateco-APM Terminals) covered the container port only.
